newsitem.title: DENMARK: New SAS cargo terminal begun in Copenhagen.
newsitem.headline: New SAS cargo terminal begun in Copenhagen.

text.p: Work began on the new Scandinavian Airlines System (SAS) cargo terminal at Copenhagen International Airport on Tuesday, with summer 1998 set as completion date.

SAS said in a statement that that the new terminal, with a total area of 24,000 square metres and annual capacity for 350,000 tonnes freight and post, would cost 300 million Danish crowns to build with a further 200 million crowns to be spent on technical installations.
Copenhagen Airports is responsible for building the terminal with SAS putting in the installations, it said.
SAS said the new cargo terminal would be more centrally located at Copenhagen International Airport than the present outdated freight hangar.
It said it planned to add an additional 5,000 square metres production area to the site at a later juncture.

"The (building) project means that we really have ambitions with SAS Cargo. The new, efficient terminal should attract even more cargo to Copenhagen," SAS Cargo director Peter Groenlund said in a statement.
